home.headline: Find the best place to watch the total eclipse in Iceland.
home.subhead: On August 12, 2026, totality lasts just over two minutes — and clouds and terrain decide who actually sees it. EclipseChase ranks every viewing spot by clear-sky odds, horizon, and totality time, so you can plan ahead and move to the best one on the day.
home.hero_rarity: The next total solar eclipse over Iceland isn't until 2196.
home.hero_pro_cta: See what Pro shows on the day →
home.hero_support_1: Clear-sky odds from 10 years of August 12 cloud history
home.hero_support_2: Horizon checked against 30 m terrain — so the sun isn't hiding behind a ridge
home.hero_support_3: Live cloud map and road cams to move when it counts
home.horizon_title: This is the check behind every recommendation.
home.horizon_body: Every viewing location runs through the same routine: a 91-ray sweep across the sun's bearing, sampled against ÍslandsDEM 30 m elevation data and corrected for Earth curvature plus atmospheric refraction. The dashed arc plots the sun's path across August 12 — the marker is totality.
home.horizon_blocked_caption: Red overlay marks every azimuth where the terrain rises above the sun's altitude. Here it covers most of the sky on the sun's bearing.
home.horizon_clear_caption: Open Atlantic horizon to the west-southwest. The sun's path stays clear of the silhouette for hours either side of totality.
home.horizon_note: Sun shown at totality — 17:46 UTC on August 12, 2026.

home.dashboard_horizon_alt: EclipseChase map with weather icons overlaid on viewing spots, showing a horizon profile chart for Ytri Tunga Beach with 24 degree sun clearance above terrain.

home.opportunity_title: You get one shot at this.
home.opportunity_body: On August 12, 2026 the Moon's shadow crosses western Iceland for just over two minutes — then it's gone for 170 years. Clouds and terrain decide who actually sees it. {emphasis} check the horizon and cloud history before you commit to a spot.
home.tricky_body: Totality runs from Snæfellsnes through Reykjanes — but the cloud history flips as you head southwest. August 12 has been clear roughly 24% of the last 10 years at Öndverðarnes, 41% at Garðskagi. You trade about 30 seconds of totality for the better odds.
home.tricky_left_caption: Westernmost tip of Snæfellsnes. Black basalt cliffs and the orange Skálasnagaviti lighthouse. Long totality, but cloud cover is more variable than Reykjanes.
home.tricky_right_caption: Northwesternmost tip of the Reykjanes peninsula, 15 minutes from Keflavík Airport. Less totality, but 4 of the last 10 August 12s have been clear or near-clear — the best odds on the path.
home.tricky_caveat: Cloud history from ERA5 reanalysis, August 12 at 17:45 UTC, 2016–2025. Past years don't guarantee 2026 conditions.

home.pro_compare_title: Free plans the trip. Pro makes the call on the day.
home.pro_compare_body: Browse every spot, totality time, horizon profile, and 10 years of cloud history for free — enough to build your shortlist before you fly. Pro turns that shortlist into a live decision on August 12: real-time cloud cover, instant horizon checks, and road cams so you can move to clearer skies.
home.pro_compare_urgency: Don't leave your one shot to chance — Pro's live scoring, horizon checks, and road cams help you move to clearer skies on the day.
home.pro_compare_price_note: One-time payment. No subscription. No account needed. Works offline through August 31, 2026.
home.pro_compare_restore_pre: Already have Pro from another device?
home.faq_a_account: No. Free features work without signup. Pro is unlocked by purchase — no email/password required. Restore on any device with your purchase email.
home.faq_q_offline: Will it work without cell coverage?
home.faq_a_offline: Yes. Pro users can download offline maps and full spot data. Essential for the Westfjords where cell service is unreliable.
home.faq_q_accuracy: How accurate are the horizon checks?
home.faq_a_accuracy: For curated viewing spots, very high — terrain at 30 m resolution (ÍslandsDEM v1.0), Skyfield-computed sun position, sampled at the spot's exact coordinates. For tap-anywhere checks on the map, your tap snaps to the nearest pre-computed grid point — typically within ~150 m on roads, up to ~2 km in the back-country. The map shows the snapped sample point whenever it's more than ~250 m from where you tapped. The verdict (clear/marginal/risky/blocked) reflects terrain only — weather is reported separately.
home.faq_a_clouds: Cloud cover in Iceland is unpredictable. We provide forecasts and live conditions; you choose. The Pro recommendation engine on the day suggests where to move based on current conditions.
home.pro_status_body: Your access works offline through August 31, 2026 — plenty of buffer after the eclipse for offline review of conditions and your photos.
home.email_body: One email when forecasts firm up. One on eclipse day with conditions. No spam.
home.email_body_pro: Optional: get an email when 7-day forecasts firm up, and another on eclipse morning summarizing best regions. Pro users also get in-app push notifications.
home.sources_terrain_body: ÍslandsDEM v1.0 from Landmælingar Íslands, CC-BY 4.0 — the only high-resolution DEM that covers Iceland (SRTM stops at 60°N). Downsampled to ~30 m for the horizon-check grid.
home.sources_weather_body: Real-time conditions and forecasts from Veðurstofa Íslands (Icelandic Meteorological Office), the national weather service.
home.sources_eclipse_body: Computed with Skyfield using JPL DE421 ephemerides — topocentric Sun and Moon positions per grid point, contact times found by bisecting their angular separation to ~1 second precision.
